title: Thirsty Celery: Parent Guide
endLine: Water climbs a plant through tiny tubes, pulled up by the leaves.

scenes.tts: How does water get to the top of a plant? A celery stalk and blue water make its path visible. You'll compare a stalk with leaves to one without.
scenes.caption: How does water get to the top of a plant? A celery stalk and blue water make its path visible. You'll compare a stalk with leaves to one without.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic kitchen counter with a tray. A tall leafy celery stalk stands in a clear glass of deep blue water, filling about 65 percent of the frame height. Large high-contrast question text above: 'How does water get to the top?' Faint blue shimmer at the base of the stalk. No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: How does water get to the top of a plant? A celery stalk and blue water make its path visible. You'll compare a stalk with leaves to one without.

scenes.visual: Same glass and stalk. Title 'Thirsty Celery' appears to the left for two seconds while the blue water ripples gently.

scenes.tts: Setting up takes about twenty minutes, plus a few short checks over a day. Your child makes a guess, waits, and checks it. They practice looking closely at something slow. And they see a path inside a plant that is normally hidden.
scenes.caption: Setting up takes about twenty minutes, plus a few short checks over a day. Your child makes a guess, waits, and checks it. They practice looking closely at something slow. And they see a path inside a plant that is normally hidden.
scenes.visual: The glass stays at right. Three labels appear one by one with small icons: 'Guess, then check' (pencil), 'Look closely' (magnifying glass), 'Wait for it' (clock with a day arc). The water ripples softly.
scenes.narration: Setting up takes about twenty minutes, plus a few short checks over a day. Your child makes a guess, waits, and checks it. They practice looking closely at something slow. And they see a path inside a plant that is normally hidden.

scenes.tts: If anyone is allergic to celery, leave it out for everyone. Use the guide's napa cabbage option instead. Keep all experiment plants out of mouths. The setup that follows is for celery. Choose food coloring everyone can use safely. If no coloring is suitable, skip the activity.
scenes.caption: If anyone is allergic to celery, leave it out for everyone. Use the guide's napa cabbage option instead. Keep all experiment plants out of mouths. The setup that follows is for celery. Choose food coloring everyone can use safely. If no coloring is suitable, skip the activity.
scenes.visual: On the same tray, show a pale napa cabbage leaf taking the place of the celery beside a sturdy clear glass. Show blue and red food coloring bottles beside the glass as alternatives.
scenes.narration: If anyone is allergic to celery, leave it out for everyone. Use the guide's napa cabbage option instead. Keep all experiment plants out of mouths. The setup that follows is for celery. Choose food coloring everyone can use safely. If no coloring is suitable, skip the activity.

scenes.tts: You need three celery stalks with leaves, three sturdy clear glasses, and blue or red food coloring. Yellow is hard to see. Add water, a tray, paper towels, and old clothes, because the coloring stains.
scenes.caption: You need three celery stalks with leaves, three sturdy clear glasses, and blue or red food coloring. Yellow is hard to see. Add water, a tray, paper towels, and old clothes, because the coloring stains.
scenes.visual: Counter cleared to a tray with paper towels. Items slide in and settle: three leafy celery stalks, three clear plastic glasses, bottles of blue and red food coloring (a yellow bottle fades in with a small X), a water jug. Label: 'Coloring stains: use a tray'.
scenes.narration: You need three celery stalks with leaves, three sturdy clear glasses, and blue or red food coloring. Yellow is hard to see. Add water, a tray, paper towels, and old clothes, because the coloring stains.

scenes.tts: Fill each glass with about five centimeters of water. Stir in fifteen to twenty drops of coloring per glass. Dark color is much easier to see.
scenes.caption: Fill each glass with about five centimeters of water. Stir in fifteen to twenty drops of coloring per glass. Dark color is much easier to see.
scenes.visual: Water fills each glass to a dashed line labeled '5 cm'. Drops fall from the bottle one after another into the first glass, with a counter label '15 to 20 drops', and the water deepens to dark blue. The other glasses follow.
scenes.narration: Fill each glass with about five centimeters of water. Stir in fifteen to twenty drops of coloring per glass. Dark color is much easier to see.

scenes.tts: You do all the cutting. Keep celery pieces and small dye caps away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Trim about two centimeters from each base just before setup. Cut all the leaves off one stalk.
scenes.caption: You do all the cutting. Keep celery pieces and small dye caps away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Trim about two centimeters from each base just before setup. Cut all the leaves off one stalk.
scenes.visual: A cutting board; an adult hand with a knife trims a short slice off a stalk base, label '2 cm, fresh cut'. A small child silhouette watches from across the board. One stalk has its leaves removed and is labeled 'no leaves'.
scenes.narration: You do all the cutting. Keep celery pieces and small dye caps away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. Trim about two centimeters from each base just before setup. Cut all the leaves off one stalk.

scenes.tts: Before they go in, hold up both stalks. Ask, 'Where do you think the blue will go?' Then ask, 'Which one will change first, the one with leaves or the one without?' Write down the guesses.
scenes.caption: Before they go in, hold up both stalks. Ask, 'Where do you think the blue will go?' Then ask, 'Which one will change first, the one with leaves or the one without?' Write down the guesses.
scenes.visual: The leafy stalk and the leafless stalk side by side, held up by schematic hands. Speech bubbles appear in turn: 'Where will the blue go?' and 'Which changes first?' A small notepad at lower left gets two check boxes, one per stalk, and stays on screen.
scenes.narration: Before they go in, hold up both stalks. Ask, 'Where do you think the blue will go?' Then ask, 'Which one will change first, the one with leaves or the one without?' Write down the guesses.

scenes.tts: Stand the leafy stalk and the leafless stalk in two glasses of the same color. Keep the third stalk as a spare. Find a bright spot out of direct sun. Stay nearby while the colored water is out.
scenes.caption: Stand the leafy stalk and the leafless stalk in two glasses of the same color. Keep the third stalk as a spare. Find a bright spot out of direct sun. Stay nearby while the colored water is out.
scenes.visual: The two stalks slide into two glasses of matching blue on the tray. A window shape with soft light appears behind them; a sun icon with a small 'not direct' mark sits outside the window.
scenes.narration: Stand the leafy stalk and the leafless stalk in two glasses of the same color. Keep the third stalk as a spare. Find a bright spot out of direct sun. Stay nearby while the colored water is out.

scenes.tts: Now a question for you. Tomorrow you will cut across the leafy stalk, above the water. What do you think the cut end will look like? Blue all over, or something else?
scenes.caption: Now a question for you. Tomorrow you will cut across the leafy stalk, above the water. What do you think the cut end will look like? Blue all over, or something else?
scenes.visual: The leafy stalk in its glass on the right. On the left a high-contrast question card: 'What will the cut end look like?' A blank round outline of a stalk cross-section sits under the card, uncolored.
scenes.narration: Now a question for you. Tomorrow you will cut across the leafy stalk, above the water. What do you think the cut end will look like? Blue all over, or something else?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and blank cross-section outline. The blue water ripples slowly and a soft ring turns beneath the question. No answer shown.

scenes.tts: Check after about one hour. Little may show yet. After about four hours, blue lines most often climb the ribs, and the leaf edges start to color. Compare the two stalks. Ask, 'Was your guess right?'
scenes.caption: Check after about one hour. Little may show yet. After about four hours, blue lines most often climb the ribs, and the leaf edges start to color. Compare the two stalks. Ask, 'Was your guess right?'
scenes.visual: In the same tray scene, advance a schematic clock to 'About 1 hour'. Hold on mostly pale stalks; if showing a faint tint, label it 'May see a faint tint'. Advance to 'About 4 hours' and reveal an example of blue ribs and leaf edges on the leafy stalk, with less color on the leafless stalk. Keep the label 'Possible result' on screen. Show the speech bubble 'Was your guess right?'
scenes.narration: Check after about one hour. Little may show yet. After about four hours, blue lines most often climb the ribs, and the leaf edges start to color. Compare the two stalks. Ask, 'Was your guess right?'

scenes.tts: The next day usually gives the clearest result, with blue veins in the leaves. Cut across the stalk about three centimeters above the water. Look for a curved row of blue dots. Each dot marks a bundle that contains water tubes.
scenes.caption: The next day usually gives the clearest result, with blue veins in the leaves. Cut across the stalk about three centimeters above the water. Look for a curved row of blue dots. Each dot marks a bundle that contains water tubes.
scenes.visual: Clock reads 'Next day': blue veins show in the leaves. An adult hand cuts across the stalk above the water. The blank cross-section outline from the question fills in: a curved row of blue dots near the outer edge, the rest pale. Label: 'Each dot: water tubes'.
scenes.narration: The next day usually gives the clearest result, with blue veins in the leaves. Cut across the stalk about three centimeters above the water. Look for a curved row of blue dots. Each dot marks a bundle that contains water tubes.

scenes.tts: Here is why the leaves matter. Water dries off through tiny pores in the leaves. As it leaves, it pulls more water up the tubes behind it. So the stalk with leaves usually colors faster.
scenes.caption: Here is why the leaves matter. Water dries off through tiny pores in the leaves. As it leaves, it pulls more water up the tubes behind it. So the stalk with leaves usually colors faster.
scenes.visual: A gentle cutaway of the leafy stalk: blue water rises in thin tubes; at the leaf, tiny dots of vapour drift out of pores into the air, and small arrows show the column moving up behind them. The leafless stalk beside it shows shorter arrows.
scenes.narration: Here is why the leaves matter. Water dries off through tiny pores in the leaves. As it leaves, it pulls more water up the tubes behind it. So the stalk with leaves usually colors faster.

scenes.tts: Stay nearby while the colored water is out. Use sturdy glasses that won't tip, kept away from toddlers and pets. Nobody eats the celery or drinks the colored water. Throw both away, and wash hands with soap.
scenes.caption: Stay nearby while the colored water is out. Use sturdy glasses that won't tip, kept away from toddlers and pets. Nobody eats the celery or drinks the colored water. Throw both away, and wash hands with soap.
scenes.visual: Safety badges beside the glasses, at most four: an adult standing near the tray, a steady plastic glass with a pet and toddler icon held back, a crossed-out mouth over a celery stalk and glass, and soapy hands under a tap.
scenes.narration: Stay nearby while the colored water is out. Use sturdy glasses that won't tip, kept away from toddlers and pets. Nobody eats the celery or drinks the colored water. Throw both away, and wash hands with soap.

scenes.tts: To finish, ask, 'Where did the water go in, and where did it go?' The color only made the path visible. With clear water, it still climbs. We just can't see it.
scenes.caption: To finish, ask, 'Where did the water go in, and where did it go?' The color only made the path visible. With clear water, it still climbs. We just can't see it.
scenes.visual: The finished leafy stalk glows softly: blue lines rising from the cut base up into blue-veined leaves, with tiny vapour dots drifting off the leaves. A speech bubble: 'Where did the water go?'
scenes.narration: To finish, ask, 'Where did the water go in, and where did it go?' The color only made the path visible. With clear water, it still climbs. We just can't see it.

scenes.line: Water climbs a plant through tiny tubes, pulled up by the leaves.
scenes.visual: End card with the blue-veined celery faint in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Water climbs a plant through tiny tubes, pulled up by the leaves.'
